rust_sdk.release_readme_finding: The exact release README identifies rmcp as the official Rust MCP SDK, states support for the stable 2026-07-28 protocol, and documents the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks SEP-2663 flow using rmcp::task_manager::TaskManager.
rust_sdk.exact_source_finding: The release TaskManager is a concrete process-memory runtime: TaskManagerInner holds a HashMap of task entries behind Arc<Mutex<...>>; spawn creates a fresh UUID task id, inserts the entry, then launches the operation with tokio::spawn; shutdown drains the map and aborts retained join handles. The inspected repository search exposed no TaskStore abstraction. ServerHandler task methods are overridable and default to method-not-found, so this is a bundled-runtime boundary, not proof that the Rust SDK protocol surface forbids a custom persistent task backend.
rust_sdk.phase1_implication: Client-persisted taskId is sufficient for disconnect/client-restart only while the same TaskManager state survives. A server-process restart loses the bundled manager state, so it is not a scheduled-Chat cross-run durable executor. Replacing it with a custom persistent task backend still requires an external resident executor/storage path and therefore remains an unresolved child under control26; it is not an accepted zero-residual Chat route.

tasks_extension_scope.relevant_spec_boundary: The extension requires task creation to be observable by tasks/get before CreateTaskResult is returned and recommends durable client-side taskId persistence for client crash/restart recovery. tasks_extension_scope.safe_claim: Protocol-level task vocabulary and immediate tasks/get observability do not by themselves prove server-process restart persistence, lost-CreateTaskResult rediscovery, execution redrive, or exactly-once external effects.

source_facts: _save_base_state serializes self with model_dump_json(exclude_none=True, context=...) and writes BASE_STATE under the installed write guard.
__setattr__ autosaves changed public fields immediately when save depth is zero; inside the context manager it defers by setting _dirty.
__exit__ flushes dirty state when save depth returns to zero, so exceptional exit does not provide rollback semantics.

leaf_event_id and head_is_empty are excluded from state-change callback emission, but last_user_message_id is not, so recovery must not replay ordinary public assignment semantics if it is intended to be silent bookkeeping.
openhands_r7.r7_commit_shape: After complete marker/event/generation validation with no public mutation, construct the final base snapshot off-object, write that snapshot exactly once under the existing write guard, then synchronize already-validated primitive recovery fields into in-memory state without passing through ConversationState.__setattr__, and only then clear recovery markers. A crash after snapshot write but before in-memory sync is safe because restart loads the committed base; a crash before write leaves the old base and marker; a crash after in-memory sync but before cleanup is idempotently recoverable from the committed base plus marker.
